musicalSources.author: Mark Gotham; Chelsey Hamm; Kris Shaffer
musicalSources.title: Open Music Theory: Simple Meter and Time Signatures
musicalSources.section: Time Signatures, Example 9; Counting in Simple Meter, Example 10 and bullets on held beats and and subdivisions
musicalSources.evidence: In 4/4 the quarter gets the beat; longer values span several beats and two eighths divide a beat into equal parts. Counting systems can differ.
musicalSources.application: Explain 1–2–3–4 while sustaining, attacks on 1/3/4 for 2–1–1, and the Russian count raz-i for even eighths.
musicalSources.limits: The Russian words, note patterns, 48/56 BPM and numerical MIDI tolerances belong to the project. No copied notation or author approval.
musicalSources.edition: Online chapter, verified 2026-11-05; no fixed print pagination asserted

implementationApplications.section: Time Signatures, Example 9; Counting in Simple Meter, Example 10 and bullets on held beats and and subdivisions
implementationApplications.application: Time Signatures, Examples 9–10: four quarter-note beats and counting through longer values. New project rhythm has bass starts 0/4/8/12 and a two-beat last note.
implementationApplications.limits: The Russian words, note patterns, 48/56 BPM and numerical MIDI tolerances belong to the project. No copied notation or author approval.

implementationApplications.section: Time Signatures, Example 9; Counting in Simple Meter, Example 10 and bullets on held beats and and subdivisions
implementationApplications.application: Examples 9–10 and counting bullets: four quarter-note beats, equal eighth subdivisions and continuing count through a half. Project pattern 1–0.5–0.5–2 is repeated in three bars.
implementationApplications.limits: The Russian words, note patterns, 48/56 BPM and numerical MIDI tolerances belong to the project. No copied notation or author approval.

implementationApplications.section: Time Signatures / Counting in Simple Meter, Examples 9–10 and rules for long notes and rests
implementationApplications.application: Count four quarter-note pulses per bar, including both two-beat internal rests. Use an explicit 32-beat project edition instead of unprepared cross-bar entrances.
implementationApplications.limits: The eight-bar project arrangement and its musical changes are editorial choices; not assigned by the source.

implementationApplications.section: Time Signatures / Counting in Simple Meter, Examples 9–10; long-note and rest counting paragraphs
implementationApplications.application: Reread continuing a four-beat count through a long note. Teach two left half notes per bar, then one whole per bar; the fourth spoken count starts the last beat rather than ending it.
implementationApplications.limits: A new hand/finger task is distinguished from the duplicated right whole-note goal; no source endorsement of the project drills or independent ear test.

implementationApplications.section: Time Signatures / Counting in Simple Meter, Examples 10–13 and paragraph on rests
implementationApplications.application: Continue the four-beat count through the unarticulated last beat. New attack at the next bar is not required to establish the end.
implementationApplications.limits: The two-C4 phrase, right-thumb assignment, 56 BPM, release allowance, ending v1 and transfer phrase are project choices; no author endorsement or independent teacher/ear-test claim.

technicalSources.author: Vercel
technicalSources.title: Web Interface Guidelines
technicalSources.section: Accessibility: async updates; Content and Copy: specific feedback
technicalSources.evidence: Async status updates should use a polite live region; feedback should explain the next action.
technicalSources.application: Announce attempt feedback as status and distinguish pending final silence from a completed attempt.
technicalSources.limits: No change to musical norms, keyboard timing measurement or physical-device validation.

systemApplications.application: Polite status feedback; no release or final-rest hint during memory attempt.

technicalSources.author: W3C; editor Michael Wilson
technicalSources.title: Web MIDI API
technicalSources.evidence: Port availability is exposed through maps, state and connection events. Section 5.6 explicitly notes that system notifications can be delayed.
technicalSources.application: Invalidate the new terminal-rest attempt on observed removal, switch, closed input or bridge interruption; recheck available state at completion.
technicalSources.limits: Does not guarantee immediate detection or actual acoustic silence; no real-device test. No new permissions or automatic MIDI connection.

nextWork.action: Пересмотреть detail-p-dyads-01..04 по первичным нотным/педагогическим источникам: C4–E4 правой 1–3, D4–F4 правой 2–4, C3–E3 левой 5–3, D3–F3 левой 4–2. Подтверждённый повод: правая 01 сейчас требует левый course03-08, а левая 03 — правую 02. Сначала сверить одновременные пары, реальные руки и подготовку в собственной пятипальцевой позиции; сохранить пользовательские якоря и редакции. Проверить обещание общего окончания двух звуков: если оно остаётся целью, применить существующий opt-in beat-boundary-v2 только с тестами отпускания, новым отпечатком и архивом прежнего прогресса. Не выдавать смену BPM или повтор за новую цель. Добавить подробные разборы и независимые фразы переноса; при недостатке источников уменьшить партию. Затем конкретизировать 1–4 подтверждённых пробела карты в будущие планы к минимуму 1000, отдельно от 1310 мест ёмкости, и продолжить необязательный компонент чтения React/Next.js. Текущий учёт: 422 записи / 158 MIDI-контрактов / 76 структурированных записей / 2 будущих плана; 415 — верхняя граница, не проверенное число самостоятельных целей.
